title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop to avoid the animal. The incident reveals a gap in how autonomous vehicles perceive and respond to small moving objects in their path, even when a human monitor is in the vehicle.

Avride investigated by reviewing vehicle data and running simulations. The company found no evidence that the vehicle failed to stop at traffic control signs, contrary to a resident's claim. The company's response was to adjust its testing area and run controlled experiments, neither of which addresses the core issue of why the system did not detect or avoid the duck. It is not established what would have enabled the vehicle to recognize the animal as an obstacle requiring evasive action.

The presence of a human safety operator did not prevent the incident. This suggests the operator either did not perceive the duck in time or was not positioned to intervene in the vehicle's motion decisions. Whether the system's training data included small animals as obstacles, or whether the vehicle was designed to treat them differently from larger objects, is not established.

Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents and intensifying their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in their area.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident. The company investigated the situation and reviewed vehicle data multiple times through simulation. While a resident claimed the car failed to stop at a stop sign, Avride stated they found no evidence supporting this claim and that the vehicle stopped appropriately at all relevant signs. In response, Avride adjusted its testing area to exclude certain streets around the lake and is now running controlled simulation experiments to improve the technology. Community members have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.
